<a id="acquire-coordinates"></a>

### Acquire coordinates

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** acquire coordinates from this linked model, so ours match the architect's.

Acquires coordinates from one linked Revit model: the link's shared system, origin and True North become this model's, based on where the link sits now. Manage > Coordinates > Acquire Coordinates - the step that puts an MEP model on the architect's survey system. **NO ELEMENT IS SHIFTED, AND WHERE EVERYTHING IS SAID TO BE CHANGES.** No element's internal position changes; every shared position, spot reading and exported position does. So the shared position of the internal origin is read BEFORE and AFTER, east/west, north/south, elevation and angle to True North, and both are reported - the evidence of what changed. **IT IS ADMIN, AND IT IS THE LINK THAT DECIDES.** A link placed in the wrong spot hands over the wrong system, and everything exported afterwards carries it. CHECK_LINK_COORDINATES is the read to run first. **A REVIT LINK ONLY.** Acquiring from a CAD link takes a different id and is not done here. Publishing INTO a link changes the linked file and is not done here either. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION (Golden Rule 16).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes project-wide settings (`ADMIN`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **link instance** - a value |
| **You get** | acquired, after, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2020 |
| **Capability** | `ACQUIRE_COORDINATES` |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. Turn **Changes and Admin** on in Heron's **Settings** (Heron tab).
3. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"acquire coordinates from the architecture link"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
4. Heron makes the change as **one entry in Revit's Undo list**. With **Ask to Keep** on, Revit asks **Keep or Discard** first; Ctrl+Z takes it back.

Other ways to ask: *"take the survey system from the linked model"* · *"get our coordinates from the architect's model"*

<a id="activate-document"></a>

### Activate document

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-24 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** make a document on disk the window in front, opening its file if it is not open, project or family alike.

Makes the document at a given path the window in front in Revit - a project or a family, already open or not. **IT EXISTS BECAUSE THERE WAS NO WAY BACK OUT OF A FAMILY.** SWITCH_ACTIVE_PROJECT moves between open PROJECTS and refuses from inside a family document: "Changing the active view is not applicable to inactive documents." So opening a family left every following fragment stuck in it - and a fragment that looks for loaded families found none, because a family document contains none. Measured 2026-09-16: five families were "opened", all five failed, and five size tables were written into the one family that happened to be in front. **THE PATH IS THE HANDLE, NOT THE TITLE.** `OpenAndActivateDocument` takes a file path and works whether or not the document is already open, which is what makes it usable as a way back: the project is always on disk, and its path is a fact the caller already has. **IT REPORTS WHAT IS IN FRONT AFTERWARDS, ALWAYS.** The whole purpose is which window is active, and the failure that matters is believing it moved when it did not - that is precisely how five tables landed in the wrong family. `activeAfter` is read back from Revit, never assumed from the argument. **IT CANNOT RUN INSIDE A TRANSACTION**, which is why it is EXECUTE. Activating a document while the current one is modifiable is refused. It changes no element in any document.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes only what Revit shows - a selection, a zoom, a view (`EXECUTE`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **document path** - text |
| **You get** | activated, active after, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |
| **Capability** | `ACTIVATE_DOCUMENT` |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"make that document the active one"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
3. Revit shows the result. Nothing in the model changes.

Other ways to ask: *"open the project file C:\Models\Tower Block.rvt"* · *"go back to the project"*

<a id="create-family-document"></a>

### Create family document

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** start a brand new family from a template and save it where I say.

Starts a new family from a family template, saves it to the file the caller names, and opens that file in a Revit window - File > New > Family, then Save As, done in one call. **VERSION 2, 2026-10-06 - SEEN AND SAVED.** Version 1 made the family in memory only. No window showed it, and nothing could save it, because SAVE_DOCUMENT refuses a document with no path rather than invent one. So every nested part of Rejin's pipe support was started by hand through File > New > Family. Now the new family is saved to exactly `savePath`, the windowless copy the API makes is closed, and the saved file is opened in a window. `title` is what the next call names it by. **THE TEMPLATE DECIDES THE CATEGORY AND ALMOST EVERYTHING ELSE**, and it is asked for rather than chosen (D-33). A full .rft path is used as given. A name alone - "Metric Generic Model" - is looked up by EXACT file name in the folder this Revit reports as its family template path, which differs by version, language and installation; the full path it used is always returned as `templateUsed`. Two files of that name are refused with both listed, and no near match is ever taken. **THE FILE NAME IS THE CALLER'S AND NOTHING IS OVERWRITTEN.** `savePath` must be a full path ending .rfa in a folder that exists. A file already there is refused and left untouched, and the save itself is told never to overwrite, so a file that appears in between is still safe. No folder is created. **SINCE VERSION 4 (D-192) HERON OPENS NO TRANSACTION GROUP IN THE MODEL IT IS AIMED AT,** because nothing in that model changes - so the new family opens in a window in this one call, the model in front or not. Heron counts that model before and after, and refuses loudly if it moved. Not yet run in Revit that way (NEEDS-CHECKING Group OX). Until then, and on an add-in built before it, the paragraph below still describes what happens: the code checks for itself and takes whichever branch is true. **WHEN HERON IS WORKING IN THE WINDOW IN FRONT, IT IS SAVED BUT NOT OPENED.** Revit opens no window while the active document is modifiable, and Heron's own transaction made it so before version 4. Measured 2026-10-06, Revit 2024: refused with "The active document is currently modifiable"; with only Heron's group open the window opened AND Revit threw an internal error; deferred to Revit's idle event it never fired. So the reply says so and gives `openNext`, the path ACTIVATE_DOCUMENT opens - that runs with no transaction and opened such a file the same day. Aimed (`--in`) at a document that is not in front, the family opens in this one call. **A PROJECT TOO, SINCE VERSION 3 - THE TEMPLATE'S EXTENSION DECIDES.** A .rte template makes a project saved as .rvt, a .rft one a family saved as .rfa; a bare template name goes by the savePath typed, and each kind looks in its own template folder. The other half must agree. Version 3 is DRAFT until proved. **IT MAKES AN EMPTY FAMILY AND NOTHING ELSE.** No geometry, no parameters, no types. The family stays open and is the caller's, like any file opened by hand. ASSUMES NOTHING ABOUT TRANSACTIONS - a new document cannot be inside the current one's, and this opens none.

| **You get** | created, title, saved to, template used, open next, findings |

| **Proved on Revit** | 2020 |

<a id="create-workset"></a>

### Create workset

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-11 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** add a new workset to this model.

Creates user worksets on a workshared model - the thing SET_ELEMENT_WORKSET needs to exist before it can put anything on one. **ADMIN risk, not MODIFY, and the reason is worth stating.** A workset is project structure that everybody on the job sees and works inside. It is named in the client's BIM execution plan, it decides what people can check out, and a stray one called "New Workset" is visible to the whole team until somebody notices. **A workset is not an element**, and this fragment is the reason to say so: it has no ElementId, so nothing downstream can be handed "the worksets that were made". What comes back is the names and whether each was created or already there. **A name that already exists is reported, never duplicated.** Revit refuses a duplicate workset name, and a batch that threw on the third of five would leave two made and three not, with nothing saying which. **On a model that is not workshared it does nothing and says so.** That is the common case for a small job, and enabling worksharing is a decision with consequences - a central file, local copies, a different way of working - so it is never done as a side effect of asking for a workset. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |
| **Capability** | `CREATE_WORKSET` |

<a id="export-model-to-nwc"></a>

### Export model to NWC

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** write the model out as a Navisworks NWC file, and check the file is really there.

Exports the model to NWC - whole document or scoped to one 3D view - and reports the path only if the file is ACTUALLY ON DISK afterwards. IT CARRIES A FACT THE OTHER EXPORTS DO NOT: THE EXPORTER MAY NOT BE THERE. NWC export comes from a separate Autodesk add-in, so a perfectly healthy Revit can simply not have it. Revit is asked FIRST, by name, and a missing exporter is reported as its own outcome rather than caught as a failure. That distinction is the fragment's reason for existing. "The export failed" and "this Revit cannot export NWC at all" lead to completely different next actions - one is worth retrying, the other needs an installer and an administrator - and an exception message buried in a log is not where somebody should have to work that out. IT DOES NOT CONSUME `elements`. NWC scope is a document or a view, never a set of elements, and taking a list only to ignore it would let a caller believe it had narrowed the export when it had not. NO TRANSACTION AND NONE IS NEEDED - unlike the IFC exporter, this one writes nothing back into the document. RISK IS **PUBLISH**. An NWC is the coordination handover; one Ctrl+Z does not un-send it.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes the model and writes files outside it (`PUBLISH`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **export folder** - text<br>**file name** - text<br>**scope view id** - the NAME of the thing, never its number - "Level 1" for a levelId. The field's own name says which kind |
| **You get** | exported path |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | none |
| **Capability** | `EXPORT_MODEL_TO_NWC` |

<a id="list-linked-models"></a>

### List linked models

**DRAFT - runs in a chat, and its answer says so.** It changes nothing in the model, so it is not refused, but it has not been proved on a real model yet.

**What it does:** which models are linked into this one, and are they actually loaded.

Reports the Revit models linked into this project - one row per linked FILE, how many times each is placed, and whether it is loaded right now. **And how each link is set, as Manage Links and the link's Properties show it (version 2):** its path type - relative or absolute, or Revit Server - and the path it was saved with; whether its type is Room Bounding; whether it is an Overlay or an Attachment; whether it is nested inside another link; whether it is unloaded for this user only. For each placement: whether it is pinned, which workset it is on, and its shared position as Revit names it. A setting that cannot be read is said, never guessed. It only reads - changing any of these is a write of its own. **Loaded is established by asking for the document, not by reading a status.** A link's stored status says what Revit last recorded; `GetLinkDocument()` returning null says the geometry is not there to read. Those two disagree after an unload, and the second one is the one that decides whether a clash check finds anything. This is the same discipline that produced TRACE_CONNECTIVITY: the flag describes intent, the geometry describes reality. **One file, several placements.** A link placed twice - a repeated wing, a mirrored block - is two instances of one file, and a list that counts instances says a project has nine linked models when it has four. The row is the file; the placement count sits on it.

<a id="list-worksets"></a>

### List worksets

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-13 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** which worksets this model has, and which of them are actually open.

Reports the model's user worksets, whether each is open, and who has it. **A closed workset is why a count comes back low, and nothing else says so.** Elements on one are not loaded at all: no view draws them, no collector returns them, nothing tallies them. Every total this library produces is a total of what is OPEN, and this fragment is what states the exclusion. **Not workshared is a third answer, not an empty one.** A single-user file has no worksets to have, which is a different condition from having none open.

<a id="read-model-file-info"></a>

### Read model file info

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-08 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** what a Revit file is, without opening it.

What a `.rvt` file actually is - which Revit saved it, whether it is a central or somebody's local, whose local, and whether their work ever reached the central - read from the file's header **without opening it**. **OPENING A MODEL TO ANSWER "WHAT VERSION IS THIS" COSTS MINUTES AND LOCKS THE FILE WHILE IT HAPPENS.** Revit writes a small header at the front of every `.rvt`, and reading it comes back in milliseconds. A folder of fifty models is a few seconds rather than an afternoon. That difference is the whole fragment. **THE ONE THAT PREVENTS REAL DAMAGE IS CENTRAL-VERSUS-LOCAL.** Opening somebody's local by mistake - or worse, detaching and saving over it - is the classic way to break a workshared job, and the file name never reliably says which it is. `isCentral` and `owner` answer before anything is opened. **AND THE ONE THAT PREVENTS A WASTED DAY IS `savedToCentral`.** False means the model somebody sent is missing work that still only exists on their machine. Nothing inside the file looks wrong; it is simply not all there, and the discovery normally happens days later. **`isNewerThanThisRevit` ANSWERS "WHY WON'T THIS OPEN" BEFORE THE FAILED ATTEMPT**, not after it. **THE VERSION VERDICT DEPENDS ON WHICH REVIT IS ASKING, AND THAT IS CORRECT.** The saved format is a fixed fact about the file; whether it counts as current is a comparison against the Revit running right now, so the same file answers differently in 2020 and in 2027. `savedFormat` is returned alongside so the verdict can be read rather than just believed.

**"CHECK THE FILES" MEANS TWO DIFFERENT JOBS AND ONE OF THEM WRITES TO DISK:** | What you meant | Use | |---|---| | "check these files before I open them", "what version is this" | `READ_MODEL_FILE_INFO`, which opens nothing and writes nothing | | "check the exported files are really there" | `EXPORT_VIEWS_TO_DWG`, which EXPORTS and then verifies what it wrote | Both fragments talk about checking files, and only one of them produces any. A request to inspect what somebody sent must not start an export. Both carry this table, for the same reason as any other pair here. **IT READS FILES, IT DOES NOT READ THE OPEN MODEL.** Nothing here touches the document in front of the user, and a path that is missing or not a Revit file is reported per file rather than ending the run - a folder check that stops at the first bad file is a folder check nobody can use.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Answers a question (`READ`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **paths** - a list - comma separated |
| **You get** | saved format, is central, owner, saved to central, is newer than this revit |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |
| **Capability** | `READ_MODEL_FILE_INFO` |

**How to use it**

<a id="reload-links"></a>

### Reload links

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** reload the links so i have the latest from the other team.

Reloads - or unloads - the linked models behind the link instances handed in. Reloading pulls in whatever the other discipline last saved, which is the first thing anybody does before coordinating. **It never REMOVES a link.** Unload drops it from memory and from every view, and it comes back with one click. Removing deletes it from the project along with anything hosted on it, and that belongs behind a deliberate delete, not behind a word that sounds similar. **One file shared by three instances reloads once.** The work is on the link TYPE, so the instances are reduced to their distinct types first - otherwise the same file is read from disk three times and the report says three. **It reads from the path Revit already has**, which is what makes it safe: it cannot point a link at a different file. Repathing a link is a different job and a bigger decision. **Revit's own result code is reported for every link, raw.** Which code comes back for a link that was already current is NOT settled here - the earlier library recorded that honestly and it stays honest. Printing what Revit actually returns is how the first real run answers it, instead of a guess hardening into a fact. **THERE IS NO UNDO - ASK FIRST, EVERY TIME, ON A REAL MODEL (version 3).** Loading and unloading a link is document management, done outside Revit's undo: Undo cannot take it back and Discard does not roll it back. An unload was measured both ways on a scratch copy - refused inside an open transaction, done for real outside one, with nothing to roll back. So before it runs on a working model the modeller is asked, and told there is no undo; when anything was done, the first finding says so again. It is proved on a scratch copy of a sample model only. It opens no transaction itself (Golden Rule 16). **AN UNLOAD IS READ BACK (version 2).** A link already unloaded is skipped and said; after unloading, the link is asked whether it is still loaded, and one that is goes to `refused`, never counted. Version 2 is DRAFT until proved.

### Rename workset

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** rename a user workset.

Renames a user workset - the tidy-up when a project's workset names stop matching the standard, or when a team name changes mid-job. **A WORKSET IS NOT AN ELEMENT, WHICH IS WHY `EDIT_TEXT_VALUES` CANNOT DO THIS.** It lives in the workset table, not in the model, and it is reached through a different object entirely. Before this fragment, asking to rename one resolved to `SET_VIEW_WORKSET_VISIBILITY` - which changes a drawing. **DELETING A WORKSET IS NOT POSSIBLE ON EVERY RELEASE THIS LIBRARY SUPPORTS, and that is checked rather than assumed.** The delete call is absent from Revit 2020's assembly and present from 2024 - read at both ends. So it is reached BY NAME, which keeps one source compiling everywhere and lets the older release report a plain reason instead of failing to build. **A NAME ALREADY IN USE IS REFUSED BY REVIT.** It is checked first, because a throw mid-rename on a workshared model is a confusing place to end up. **ON A MODEL THAT IS NOT WORKSHARED THERE ARE NO USER WORKSETS**, and that is reported rather than thrown. An empty result there means the question does not apply. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="report-addin-data"></a>

### Report addin data

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-08 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** what other add-ins have written into this file, where nothing in Revit's interface shows it.

Lists every Extensible Storage schema this Revit session carries - its name, the vendor who defined it, whether we are allowed to read it, its fields where we are - and counts how many elements in THIS model actually hold data of that shape. It changes nothing. **EXTENSIBLE STORAGE IS THE FOURTH PLACE DATA HIDES, AND THIS LIBRARY WAS LOOKING IN THREE.** Parameters, project information and element properties are all visible in Revit's own interface, so a modeller can find them by clicking. An add-in can instead define a *schema* - a shape with a GUID - and attach an entity of that shape to an element, or to an invisible document-wide record. The value is then inside the `.rvt` with nothing in the interface showing it. That is where a coordination tool keeps its own ids, where a manufacturer's add-in keeps a product code, and where a tool records *"I have processed this"*. `REPORT_PARAMETER_INVENTORY` lists every parameter an element carries and would list none of this. **A SCHEMA CAN REFUSE TO BE READ, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN, NOT A FAULT.** Each one carries a read and a write access level - public, vendor or application. A vendor-level schema is readable only by code signed with that vendor's id, so `ReadAccessGranted()` comes back false here and the FIELDS stay hidden. The schema's name, vendor, GUID and carrier count are still visible, which is normally the question anyway. **The refusal is reported and obeyed.** The access level is another vendor's decision about their own data; there is no option here for getting round it and there should not be. **SCHEMAS ARE SESSION-WIDE AND CARRIERS ARE PER-MODEL, WHICH IS THE WHOLE READING OF THE OUTPUT.** `ListSchemas()` returns every schema any loaded add-in has registered in this Revit session, including ones with no data in this file at all. A schema with zero carriers means *an add-in is installed*; a schema with carriers means *this model has been written to*. Those are different facts and dropping the empty ones would hide the difference, so both are listed and each is labelled. **THE INVISIBLE DOCUMENT-WIDE RECORD IS RECOGNISED BY TYPE NAME, NOT BY A CAST, AND THAT IS A COMPILER CONSTRAINT RATHER THAN A STYLE CHOICE.** Data that belongs to the model as a whole rather than to any element usually sits on a `DataStorage` element, which is not selectable and has no category. That type is public-looking and NOT publicly accessible - naming it is a compile error on every release here, checked on 2020 on 2026-09-05 by naming it and reading the error. So the carrier is identified by `GetType().Name` and described in words, which costs nothing and compiles everywhere. **COUNTING CARRIERS IS ONE COLLECTOR PASS PER SCHEMA**, so a model with many schemas pays for it. `countCarriers` off gives the schema list alone, and the summary says which of the two questions was answered.

<a id="report-coverage"></a>

### Report coverage

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-13 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** how much floor does each diffuser actually serve.

Reports what each point-based element covers at a stated radius - the area each one serves, the total, and how far each is from its nearest neighbour. Built for air terminals and it works for anything placed on a grid: lights, sprinklers, detectors, sockets. **THE RADIUS IS THE CALLER'S AND THERE IS NOTHING IN THE MODEL TO READ IT FROM.** A diffuser carries flow, pressure drop and neck size; it does not carry a coverage. What one covers is a design decision - a throw at a velocity, a code spacing, a lighting level - and a fragment that invented one would put a number nobody chose into a layout somebody signs. **THE TOTAL IS AN UPPER BOUND, NOT AN ANSWER, AND OVERLAPS ARE WHY.** Circles that overlap are counted twice in a sum. The total is still worth having against a room's area - if it is BELOW the floor area there are certainly gaps - but a total above it proves nothing. Said here rather than left for somebody to work out from a number that looks like a result. **THE NEAREST-NEIGHBOUR DISTANCE IS WHERE THE GAPS SHOW.** Two elements further apart than twice the radius cannot overlap, so there is floor between them nothing covers. That comparison is the one that finds a hole in a layout, and it is reported per element. ASSUMES NOTHING ABOUT TRANSACTIONS - it opens none and needs none.

<a id="report-external-references"></a>

### Report external references

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-13 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** every file this model needs, and whether Revit can find it right now.

Every file this model depends on in one list - Revit links, CAD links and imports, point clouds, keynote tables, IFC links - what kind each is, where it points, and whether Revit can currently resolve it. **IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT A LIST OF REVIT LINKS.** Collecting `RevitLinkInstance` is the obvious implementation and it reports a model whose real risk is three unresolved DWGs and a point cloud as CLEAN. Revit keeps one list of all of them and that is what is read here, so a handover checklist built from this cannot be short by a category nobody thought to ask about. **THERE ARE TWO PATHS PER REFERENCE AND THEY ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS.** One is what the file SAVED, which may be relative. The other is what it currently RESOLVES TO on this machine. When a link goes missing after a move, the saved path is usually still correct and the resolved one has gone stale - so reporting only one of them names the wrong thing as broken. Both are returned. **"NOT LOADED" IS NOT "BROKEN", AND THERE ARE THREE WAYS TO BE NOT LOADED.** The status enum carries seven values and the useful split is not the obvious two-way one: | Status | Meaning | Where it goes | |---|---|---| | `Unloaded` | unloaded for everyone | `unloaded` | | `LocallyUnloaded` | unloaded by this user only | `unloaded` | | `InClosedWorkset` | its workset is closed this session | `unloaded` | | `NotFound` | the file is not where the model expects | `unresolved` | | `Invalid` | the reference itself is broken | `unresolved` | | `CanBeUpgraded` | loaded, from an older Revit | neither | Treating everything that is not `Loaded` as broken puts three false alarms on a handover checklist, and a checklist with false alarms stops being read - the same outcome as not writing one. **AN IMPORT IS NOT A LINK, AND IT APPEARS HERE ANYWAY.** A CAD file brought in with Import rather than Link is embedded: there is no external file left to lose, so it can never go missing, and it bloats the model instead. It is reported with its kind so the two problems stay apart - one travels, the other weighs. **A CLOUD-HOSTED REFERENCE HAS NO LOCAL PATH**, and reports its cloud identity instead. That is the correct answer for it, not a failure to resolve, and treating an empty path as missing would report every cloud-hosted project as broken.

<a id="report-geometry-complexity"></a>

### Report geometry complexity

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-09 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** which families are making this model slow, measured rather than guessed.

Measures how much geometry each family TYPE actually carries - as a triangle count, at every detail level - and ranks the types by what they cost the model once their instances are counted. The answer to *"the model has got heavy and nobody knows why"*, and the check to run on a downloaded manufacturer family before it enters the library. It changes nothing. **TRIANGLES, NOT FILE SIZE, BECAUSE DRAWING IS WHAT COSTS.** A family's file size says what it weighs on disk. What slows Revit down is what it has to DRAW: every face of every solid, tessellated into triangles, for every instance in every open view. `Face.Triangulate().NumTriangles` is that number directly. A cast-in sleeve with a modelled thread can carry more triangles than an air handling unit, and neither its name nor its size hints at it. **MEASURED PER TYPE AND MULTIPLIED BY THE INSTANCES, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT.** Geometry belongs to the type, so four hundred instances of a twelve-thousand-triangle family is 4.8 million triangles from ONE library choice. The type's own count is not what hurts; the product is, and the ranking is on the product. **ALL THREE DETAIL LEVELS ARE MEASURED, BECAUSE THE COMPARISON IS THE ACTIONABLE PART.** A family reading 40 triangles coarse and 40,000 fine is BEHAVING - it has proper detail-level control and costs nothing on a working plan. A family with the same large number at all three has none, and pays full price in every view. That gap says whether to fix the family or replace it, and one number alone says neither. **IT IS A COMPARISON, NOT A SCORE, AND THE READ-BACK SAYS SO.** Revit's tessellation is what it decides at the moment of asking, not a stored property. The numbers rank families against each other honestly and mean nothing as absolutes, so no threshold is built in and none should be read into them. **A TYPE THAT COULD NOT BE MEASURED IS NAMED, NEVER SCORED ZERO.** A family whose geometry does not come back - a face-hosted void, a corrupt type, a category whose geometry is view-specific - is listed as unmeasured. Reporting it as zero would put the heaviest thing in the model at the bottom of the ranking and read as good news. **THE COST OF ASKING IS REAL AND IS CAPPED.** Reading geometry three times per distinct type is genuine work, so `maxTypes` stops a whole-model run running away, and the summary says how many types were left unmeasured by the cap rather than quietly truncating the ranking.

<a id="report-material-takeoff"></a>

### Report material takeoff

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-13 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** how much of each material is in these elements.

Area and volume of each material across a set of elements, taken from Revit's own takeoff engine rather than recomputed from geometry - so the numbers agree with a Material Takeoff schedule instead of being a second opinion nobody can reconcile. **PAINT AND GEOMETRY ARE TWO SEPARATE MATERIAL SETS AND ASKING FOR ONE MISSES THE OTHER ENTIRELY.** An element's geometric and compound-structure materials are one set. Materials applied face by face with Paint are a different set, reached by a different flag - and the area call must be given the SAME flag it was listed with. Read only the geometry set and a painted finish reports as ZERO, which on a finishes schedule reads as *"that material is not in this model"* rather than *"I did not ask for it"*. Both sets are read, and `paintedMaterials` says which came from where. **PAINT HAS AREA AND NEVER VOLUME.** Paint is a surface, not a body, so there is no volume to ask for. A painted material therefore has an area and NO volume entry, and that absence is the correct answer rather than missing data. It is also why the result is not sorted by volume anywhere - doing so buries every painted finish at the bottom of a finishes schedule. **THE NUMBERS ARE REVIT'S, NOT THIS FRAGMENT'S.** Nothing is derived from solids here. That is deliberate: a takeoff computed independently produces a defensible figure that disagrees with the model's own schedule, and two numbers that both look right is worse than one that is plainly wrong. **IT ALSO SAYS WHAT EACH ELEMENT IS MADE OF** (version 2, when READ_ELEMENT_MATERIAL was merged in): `materials` names every material of each element, painted ones included, `noMaterial` the elements carrying none, and the totals come in cubic and square metres beside Revit's own units. An element handed in twice is taken off once. **AND THE EMBODIED CARBON, WHEN A FACTOR IS NAMED** (version 3): each material's volume times the carbon factor stored on the material, grouped by material, category or type, largest first - the hotspots lead - with the materials that have no factor named rather than counted as zero.

|---|---|
| **Kind** | Answers a question (`READ`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **Works on** | what is selected in Revit: elements |
| **You say** | **factor parameter** - text; optional, left out means *none*<br>**group by** - text; optional, left out means *material*<br>**top** - a whole number - digits only - 250, not 250mm; optional, left out means *0* |
| **You get** | areas, volumes, painted materials, materials, volume m3, area m2, carbon, total kg, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |
| **Capability** | `REPORT_MATERIAL_TAKEOFF` |

<a id="report-open-documents"></a>

### Report open documents

**DRAFT - runs in a chat, and its answer says so.** It changes nothing in the model, so it is not refused, but it has not been proved on a real model yet.

**What it does:** which projects and families are open in this Revit, each with its file or none yet and when that file was last saved, and how to tell two models of the same name apart.

Lists the projects open in this Revit session, and the families open in the Family Editor, with enough identity to act on one: each model's title and full path, and each family's category and file, or that it has none yet. It changes nothing. **THIS EXISTS BECAUSE A TITLE IS NOT AN IDENTIFIER.** Two projects called `Project1` can be open at once, and then *"switch to Project1"* names nothing. Revit's own tab bar has the same problem and solves it by making you look. So the full **path** is reported beside every title, and it is the path ACTIVATE_DOCUMENT takes to bring one to the front - a title is the convenience, the path is the answer. **A FAMILY BEING EDITED IS NOT A PROJECT.** Each one is listed apart, on one line in `familyList`, and one with no file is said to be NEVER SAVED: nothing on disk holds it. **LINKS ARE COUNTED, NOT LISTED.** `Application.Documents` returns each linked model too, and a link is nothing to switch to. **AN UNSAVED PROJECT HAS NO PATH, AND THAT IS NOT AN ERROR.** A new model that has never been saved reports an empty `PathName`, said out loud rather than left blank: such a project can only ever be matched by title. **A SAVE IS CHECKED ON DISK, NOT TRUSTED.** Each document with a file has the time its file was last written, and how long ago, in `fileTimes`. One with unsaved changes and a file more than fifteen minutes old is said out loud with that time - *the file on disk is from 10:42 - everything since is not saved* - because Ctrl+S pressed while another window is in front saves nothing, and "[unsaved changes]" alone cannot tell five minutes of work from a whole tower. Read again after a save, the time is now. Reads only. Opens no transaction and needs none.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Answers a question (`READ`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You get** | documents, paths, titles, active title, count, family list, family count, file times, stale file count, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | none |
| **Capability** | `REPORT_OPEN_DOCUMENTS` |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"what projects are open"*.
3. Heron answers in the chat. Nothing in the model changes.

Other ways to ask: *"which models are open right now"* · *"list the open Revit files"*

<a id="report-phases"></a>

### Report phases

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-13 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** the project's phases, in order, with the exact names to use.

Every phase in the project, in the order Revit holds them, with the exact name and id of each. **IT IS THE DISCOVERY STEP FOR EVERY PHASE JOB**, and without it those jobs are guesses. `SET_ELEMENT_PHASE` needs an exact existing phase name; so does anything that renames or deletes one. A near-miss - *"Existing"* against *"Existing Construction"* - fails or, worse, matches something else. Nothing in Revit's own UI hands over that list in a form anything can use. **THE ORDER IS INFORMATION, NOT PRESENTATION.** Phases are sequential and Revit keeps them so: *"the phase before this one"* and *"the last phase"* are real ideas that only the order can answer. It is returned as Revit holds it and never sorted by name, which would put *"Phase 10"* between *"Phase 1"* and *"Phase 2"*. **A MODEL WITH ONE PHASE IS THE COMMON CASE AND IS NOT A FINDING.** Most projects never leave the default, and reporting that as something to look at wastes the reader's attention on the majority of models.

<a id="save-document"></a>

### Save document

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-24 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** save an open document to its own file, and close its window - the model Heron is changing too, once its change is kept.

Saves an open document - a family built in its own window, a tyre for a car - to the file it was opened from, named by that file's path, and closes its window when asked, so the family it belongs in can load it. Since version 3 it also saves the model Heron is changing: to its own file, or - never saved yet - as the full path the modeller typed. **THE MODEL HERON IS CHANGING IS SAVED BY THE ADD-IN, ONCE HERON'S UNDO ENTRY HAS CLOSED** (version 3, Q-69, D-171). Revit will not save a document while Heron's Undo entry is open in it, so this card never saves that one itself - version 1 tried to, which Revit always refuses (row 5b-365). It asks the add-in through `saveWhenKept`, and the reply's `save` block says what the add-in wrote. **A kept change is saved, and so is a preview**: the preview's change is rolled back and its save is NOT - the reply says both, and that a save cannot be undone. **A Discard saves nothing**: the box is answered before the save, so a save follows only a Keep. A model that has a file keeps its name; a new one goes only to the path given, replacing a file there only with `replaceFile=true`, and the chat follows the model to its new name. Heron never closes that model's window. **ANOTHER OPEN DOCUMENT IS SAVED THE SAME WAY, AFTER THE GROUP** (row 5b-1824): the card asks the add-in through `saveOtherWhenKept`, and the add-in saves it to its own file and then closes its window when asked - after a Keep, and after a preview; **a Discard saves and closes nothing**. Until 2026-11-16 this card saved it inside the run, before the Keep or Discard box. The card itself writes and closes nothing. **A LOCAL SAVE OF A WORKSHARED MODEL IS NOT A SYNC.** It reaches nobody else on the job, so it says so - `SYNC_WITH_CENTRAL` is the other job. The CENTRAL model opened directly is refused, and nothing here synchronises. **IT IS `PUBLISH` RISK AND IT IS NOT UNDOABLE.** It never chooses a file name: another document with no file is not found here at all. **ONLY A WINDOW THAT IS NOT IN FRONT CAN BE CLOSED.** Revit lets no tool close the window in front, so that one is saved and left open for the modeller to close, and nothing with unsaved changes is ever closed.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes the model and writes files outside it (`PUBLISH`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **document path** - text; optional<br>**save as path** - text; optional<br>**replace file** - yes or no - true or false; optional<br>**close window** - yes or no - true or false; optional |
| **You get** | save asked, save asked to, close asked, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |
| **Capability** | `SAVE_DOCUMENT` |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.

Other ways to ask: *"save this file"* · *"save my changes"*

<a id="set-design-option"></a>

### Set design option

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** put these elements into a design option, and say plainly when Revit will not let you.

Puts elements from the main model into a named design option, and refuses - clearly, naming the manual step - when Revit's own API makes that impossible. The write counterpart to `REPORT_DESIGN_OPTIONS`, which can say what options exist and what is inside them but cannot put anything there. **`Element.DesignOption` IS READ-ONLY, SO THERE IS NO "REASSIGN" CALL AND THIS FRAGMENT DOES NOT PRETEND OTHERWISE.** The only route the API leaves is the one Revit's own interface ultimately uses: with the target option ACTIVE, copy the elements in place. The copies belong to the option; the originals stay in the main model, untouched. The read-back says exactly that, because *"added to the option"* would describe a move that did not happen. **NO PUBLIC API CAN MAKE A DESIGN OPTION ACTIVE, AND THAT REFUSAL IS THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE.** The earlier library recorded a full search: every member matching *"ActiveDesignOption"* anywhere on `Document` or `DesignOption` is the read-only `DesignOption.GetActiveDesignOptionId`, there is no setter on either, and the option-set class is internal. The postable commands open a dialog with no way to pass a target. So this fragment CHECKS which option is active and stops with the exact menu path when it is not the right one - rather than copying into whichever option happened to be active, which is a wrong answer that looks like a right one. **IT NEVER ACTIVATES OR DEACTIVATES ANYTHING, INCLUDING AFTERWARDS.** Since it cannot set the active option, it must not clear the one the modeller deliberately set up before running it. **`deleteOriginals` WAS NOT CARRIED OVER, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.** The earlier version could delete the main-model originals afterwards to simulate a move. Copying and deleting are two jobs: composing `DELETE_ELEMENTS` after this one makes the deletion visible in the operation, reviewable on its own, and refusable on its own. Folding it into a flag hides the most destructive half of the work behind a boolean. **IT OPENS NO TRANSACTION.** Golden Rule 16 - the caller's transaction covers the copy, so the copy and whatever else is in the same operation are one undo entry.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes the model (`MODIFY`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **Works on** | what is selected in Revit: elements |
| **You say** | **design option name** - text |
| **You get** | findings, new element ids, copied |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | none |
| **Capability** | `SET_DESIGN_OPTION` |

Once it is proved, you will ask: *"put these elements into a design option"* · *"add this to design option B"* · *"move these into the alternative option"*

<a id="set-link-room-bounding"></a>

### Set link room bounding

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** make the linked model room bounding, so rooms and spaces see its walls.

Switches Room Bounding on or off for one Revit link or every link - the link type's own setting that lets this model's rooms and MEP spaces stop at the linked model's walls, floors and ceilings. **AND HOW EACH LINK STORES ITS PATH** (version 2) - Relative or Absolute, as Manage Links' Path Type column does; a Revit Server or cloud link is named and left alone. Either setting, or both, in one call. **IT IS THE REASON SPACES WILL NOT PLACE IN AN MEP MODEL.** An MEP model draws no walls of its own; its spaces are bounded by the architect's link, and only when that link is Room Bounding. PLACE_ROOMS and SYNC_SPACES_WITH_LINKED_ROOMS both find unbounded spaces when it is off, and until this fragment nothing could switch it. **IT IS A TYPE SETTING**, so every placed copy of that link changes with it, and each link type is read back after the change, never assumed. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION (Golden Rule 16). One call is one undo entry.

**What it does:** change the units, symbol and rounding the project shows a kind of value in.

Changes Manage > Project Units: switches any unit type - length, area, volume, cooling load, heating load, air flow, temperature and the rest - to other units, another symbol or another rounding, each named in Revit's own words, and changes the decimal symbol / digit grouping. One table of changes - "Cooling Load=Btu/h; Air Flow=CFM; Length=Millimeters, 0 decimal places" - with every value read back after the one write. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="set-worksharing-ownership"></a>

### Set worksharing ownership

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** check out these worksets for the current user, or relinquish all mine, without sending my edits to central.

On a workshared model, takes ownership of named user worksets for the current user - Revit's Make Editable - or gives back every element and workset the user owns and has not edited - Relinquish All Mine - without sending any edits to central. **IT REACHES THE CENTRAL MODEL, SO IT IS PUBLISH.** Taking a workset stops everybody else editing it; giving it back lets them. Neither is undone by Undo, and Revit refuses both inside a transaction - this opens none. **WHAT WAS ASKED IS NOT WHAT WAS GOT.** Revit takes as many of the worksets as it can; one owned by somebody else stays theirs. Each workset asked for is read back afterwards - owned by this user, or by whom - never assumed. **ONLY WHAT IS UNCHANGED IS RELINQUISHED.** An element edited and not yet sent to central stays owned - Revit's rule - so the count given back can be smaller than what is owned. SYNC_WITH_CENTRAL is how edits reach central. **A MODEL THAT IS NOT WORKSHARED IS REFUSED BY NAME.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes the model and writes files outside it (`PUBLISH`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **action** - text<br>**workset names** - text |
| **You get** | changed, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | none |
| **Capability** | `SET_WORKSHARING_OWNERSHIP` |

Once it is proved, you will ask: *"make my workset editable"* · *"check out the mechanical workset"* · *"relinquish everything I own"*

<a id="sync-with-central"></a>

### Sync with central

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** send my changes to the central model and take everybody else's.

Synchronises a workshared model with its central file, and says what it relinquished. **NOTHING IN HERON COULD SAVE OR SYNC ANYTHING.** Measured 2026-09-18 across every fragment AND the whole add-in: `SynchronizeWithCentral` appears nowhere, and `Document.Save` appears nowhere. The only `SaveAs` calls are for family files and print settings. So Heron could read who owns what (`REPORT_ELEMENT_OWNERSHIP`), report what may be edited (`REPORT_ELEMENT_OWNERSHIP`), and then modify a workshared model and leave every change sitting in somebody's local file waiting for a hand on the keyboard. **IT IS `PUBLISH` RISK, WHICH IS THE POINT RATHER THAN A FORMALITY.** A sync pushes work to everybody on the job. It cannot be undone, it can take minutes, and it can surface another person's conflicting edits. Phase 0 and Phase 1 refuse `PUBLISH` unconditionally, so this is written and deliberately unreachable until the register says otherwise - which is the right order. **IT RELINQUISHES WHAT IT OWNS AND SAYS SO.** Syncing without relinquishing leaves elements checked out under somebody's name after they have walked away, and the next person gets a refusal they cannot explain. What was given up is reported rather than assumed. **A MODEL THAT IS NOT WORKSHARED IS REFUSED BY NAME.** There is no central file to sync with and the call would throw; the refusal says which, because "sync failed" on a single-user model reads as a broken tool. OPENS NO TRANSACTION AND MUST NOT BE INSIDE ONE. Revit refuses a sync within a transaction, which is the opposite of Golden Rule 16's usual shape and is worth stating because every other write fragment here assumes one.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes the model and writes files outside it (`PUBLISH`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **comment** - text<br>**relinquish** - yes or no - true or false |
| **You get** | synchronised, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | none |
| **Capability** | `SYNC_WITH_CENTRAL` |

Once it is proved, you will ask: *"sync with central"* · *"synchronise the model"* · *"push my changes to central"*

<a id="upgrade-family-files"></a>

### Upgrade family files

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-11 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** upgrade this library of families to the Revit we are running.

Opens each family, template or project file given, saves it into a destination folder under the running Revit, and closes it - the batch version of open-it-and-press-Save-As, for a library that has to move to a new release. **IT WORKS BECAUSE A FILE OPENED THIS WAY HAS NO WINDOW.** Revit will not let an add-in save the document somebody is looking at; a document opened through the application rather than the interface is a background document with no window, and it saves normally. Each file is opened, saved and closed before the next one starts, so memory does not climb through a large library. **IT ALWAYS WRITES SOMEWHERE ELSE, AND THERE IS NO IN-PLACE MODE.** An upgrade is one-way: once a file is saved by a newer Revit, the older Revit can never open it again. Overwriting the originals destroys the only copy that still works for everyone left on the old version - a colleague, a consultant, an archive. A destination that resolves to the source file is refused per file rather than warned about. **A WORKSHARED PROJECT IS DETACHED BEFORE IT IS TOUCHED, AND A PROJECT WHOSE WORKSHARING CANNOT BE READ IS REFUSED.** Opened without saying otherwise, a central file opens AS the central - and upgrading and saving from there is a genuinely damaging thing to do to a live job. Detaching means the copy on disk is untouched and the open document cannot write back to the central at all. The file is asked first whether it is workshared, because asking to detach a file that is not workshared is itself refused; and if that question cannot be answered on a project file, the file is skipped rather than opened hopefully. **WORKSETS ARE OPENED, NOT CLOSED, AND THAT IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE USUAL ADVICE.** A read-only pass over a big model closes worksets for speed. An upgrade has to rewrite every element in the file, so a closed workset leaves its content unconverted - the file reports as upgraded and part of it is not. **THE THUMBNAIL IS SET DELIBERATELY, BECAUSE IT IS HOW A FAMILY LIBRARY IS ACTUALLY USED.** A file's preview comes from one nominated view. Save without saying which and the upgraded copy can come out blank, and a library browsed by thumbnail in Revit's own dialog becomes unnavigable. Whatever the file already nominated is kept; failing that a 3D view, failing that a plan - and each candidate is checked against Revit's own test first, because handing it a view that cannot be a preview makes the save throw. **THE FILE IS COMPACTED ON THE WAY OUT.** The upgrade is the one moment the whole file is rewritten anyway, so it costs nothing extra, and it is the difference between a library that grows every release and one that does not. **PROJECT FILES ARE OFF UNLESS ASKED FOR.** Families and templates upgrade cleanly. A project is a decision about a job rather than a maintenance task, and it is turned on explicitly. **ONE FILE FAILING DOES NOT STOP THE BATCH.** A family that will not upgrade usually will not for a real reason - a corrupt nested family, a missing type catalogue - and the message is kept against that file while the rest continue. **IT IS SLOW AND REVIT IS BUSY THROUGHOUT.** `maxFiles` is a brake, not a formality: seconds per file means a real library is minutes, and the first batch should be small enough to open two of the results by hand. ASSUMES NO TRANSACTION AND MUST NOT BE RUN INSIDE ONE. It does not touch the open model at all; it opens and closes other documents, which a transaction on this one has no business wrapping.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes the model and writes files outside it (`PUBLISH`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **source files** - a list - comma separated<br>**destination folder** - text<br>**allow project files** - yes or no - true or false<br>**max files** - a whole number - digits only - 250, not 250mm |
| **You get** | upgraded, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |
| **Capability** | `UPGRADE_FAMILY_FILES` |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. Turn **Changes and Publish** on in Heron's **Settings** (Heron tab).
3. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"upgrade our family library"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
4. Heron makes the change as **one entry in Revit's Undo list**. With **Ask to Keep** on, Revit asks **Keep or Discard** first; Ctrl+Z takes it back.

Other ways to ask: *"move these families to the new Revit version"* · *"batch save as for this folder of families"*
